newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to probe Thomson Multimedia aid.
newsitem.headline: EU to probe Thomson Multimedia aid.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to start a formal probe on Wednesday into the recapitalisation of Thomson SA's multimedia unit, Commission sources said on Friday.
The Commission was initially assessing the recapitalisation of the entire state-owned defence and consumer electronics giant prior to its planned sale to Lagardere and Daewoo Electronics.

But it decided to split the file following the French government's decision earlier this month to cancel the group's privatisation. Thomson-CSF is now set to be sold early in 1997, but debt-laden Thomson Multimedia will first be restructured.
"We will start the (state aid) procedure on Thomson Multimedia. For the rest, we will see later," one EU source said.

Before Thomson's sale was cancelled, France had requested the Commission's permission to inject some 11 billion francs ($2.1 billion) in the loss-making group, the "major part" of which was due to benefit the multimedia division, Commission sources said recently.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis has also been reported as saying that TMM would get 9.9 billion francs.

The Commission usually starts a probe if it suspects that the recapitalisation of a state-owned company involves public subsidies. In return for its approval, it normally asks that the company being aided be restructured so as to ensure its long-term viability and insists that its market share be frozen for the duration of the restructuring plan to avoid unfair competition.

The opening of the procedure also gives third parties the oportunity to make comments. Philips Electronics has already made it known to the Commission that it is carefully watching how it deals with TMM.
At the end of 1995, TMM had debts of 13.8 billion francs. $1 = 5.20 francs -- Amelia Torres 32 2 2876841
